claims.text: Boride-based components are currently used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment without additional surface modification.
A thin, dense diffusion-barrier coating can be applied to boride-based components.
A silicide or advanced ceramic layer is a suitable diffusion-barrier coating for this application.
The proposed coating can be deposited by physical vapor deposition or pack cementation.
The relevant service environment involves direct, prolonged contact with molten aluminum above 660°C.
The coating will form an intact, adherent protective interface between the boride substrate and molten aluminum.
Dense surface films can improve resistance to high-temperature environmental attack.
The coating will inhibit interdiffusion of aluminum into the boride substrate.
The coating will limit interfacial chemical reactions that cause molten-aluminum corrosion.
Physical isolation by the coating will reduce exposure of the boride phase to molten aluminum.
Coated boride components will have a significantly lower corrosion rate than otherwise identical uncoated components.
The lower corrosion rate will be observable as reduced weight loss and improved microstructural integrity.
Improved molten-aluminum corrosion resistance will extend component service life.
Protection will persist only while the coating remains intact, adherent, and chemically stable at the operating temperature.
The magnitude of improvement and long-term durability under cyclic thermal and chemical stresses are uncertain.
